problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2$, equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3).
$$

 Find $⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$, if

$$
x(t)={t}^{2}-2t-3,\,y(t)={t}^{2}-1.
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Inner Product of Two Vectors in a Vector Space of Polynomials
examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathbb{R}_2[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2$, equipped with the inner product 

$$
\langle {x}(t), {y}(t) \rangle = x(1)y(1) + x(2)y(2) + x(3)y(3).
$$

 Find $\langle \mathbf{x}(t), \mathbf{y}(t) \rangle,$ if

$$
{x}(t) = 1-2t+3t^2,
	\quad
	{y}(t) = t-t^2.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Computing the inner product according to the definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & =x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3) \\  & =2\cdot 0+9\cdot (-2)+22\cdot (-6) \\  & =0-18-132 \\  & =-150.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is given by $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+5{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ Find $⟨x,y⟩$, if

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Computing the inner product according to the definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+5{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =(-1)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (0)+5\cdot 0\cdot 1 \\  & =-2+0+0 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
